full_judgment: 5. The co-applicant opposite-party No.1 without compliance of the Order No. 25 dated 4-6-2001 passed by the Court filed Civil Revision No. 3977 of 2001 before this Court on 22-7-2001 and obtained Rule and the order of stay of the operation of the Order No. 25 dated 4-6-2001. In that revision application the opposite party No.1 said the sub-section 6 of section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 makes no provision for making statutory deposit before the final determination for the claim of the co-applicant and the High Court Division did not accept the contention of the prayer of the petitioner of the revision application and held that under section 96(6) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act the co-applicant is required to make the statutory deposit within the time allowed by the Court and no where in the scheme of section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act it has been spelt out that the co-applicant can make the necessary deposit after the final determination of his claim by the Court. Such an argument appears to be totally misconceived and preposterous. under sub-section 96(1) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act making the statutory deposit a condition precedent for filing pre-emption case but is not so in the case of an application under section 96(4) of the said Act. In the latter case, the co-applicant is required to make the necessary deposit within the time allowed by the Court after his prayer to be joined as a co-applicant has been allowed by the Court. If he fails to comply with the order of the Court in making the deposit within the time given by the Court, his application under section 96(6) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act shall stand rejected.
